title: Heatmap root-cause journal: token-position latency spike
content:
Purpose:
This is a running investigation journal for a persistent p99 -> p99.9 latency spike observed in the serving runtime in late Sep 2025. The goal: capture what we tried, why we tried it, quick experiment logs, and final hypotheses so rollbacks / mitigations are quick and reproducible. Treat as working notes — rough, chopped, and full of TODOs.

Summary of symptom:
- Metric: per-route token-latency heatmap shows a band of high latency for token positions 180-240 (sequence-normalized) on long-context chat sessions.
- Spike shape: narrow vertical band in heatmap repeated across multiple models (gptx-13b-compat, open-7b-v2) but not all traffic. p50/p90 unchanged; p99 and tail show step up ~3x for those token indices.
- Onset: first alert 2025-09-27 03:20 UTC; increase correlates with a minor runtime release (rolling kernel/optimization) 2025-09-27 01:12 UTC (candidate).

Quick actionable hypothesis list (ranked):
1) kernel selection change or new fused-kernel introduced that regresses mid-sequence time due to kernel launch overhead for certain sequence lengths.
2) batching algorithm changes create misaligned batch boundaries around 180-240 token lengths causing an extra KV-copy or cache flush.
3) memory allocator change (jemalloc/fragmentation) causing occasional stall when contiguous region crosses threshold.
4) rare CPU-side scheduling interference when attention window crosses a threshold and triggers a different codepath.

Important context/constraints:
- Affected: hosted API and some Dedicated pools running the updated runtime image; Private deployments not showing it (helps isolate to code change in runtime, not models).
- Canary: our canary program did not catch this: canary traffic is short-context (~64 tokens) so the bug didn't surface. Need to change canary traffic shapes.

Data sources we used:
- heatmap panel (route X / model Y) on Console -> token-latency-heatmap
- p99 timeline and alert window traces (Trace IDs collected in alert payload)
- flamegraphs from CPU profiler (perf + async-profiler) and GPU timelines (nsight/cupti traces) for sampled requests
- continuous-benchmark snapshots around release times (snapshot ids: snap-2025-09-26, snap-2025-09-27)
- request-sample dump from sample-request-collector (sampled requests with tokenization and metadata)

Investigation steps + notes (chronological):
2025-09-27 03:45 — initial triage (me):
- Pulled heatmap and overlaid release timestamps — vertical band aligns with release-2025-09-27-a.
- Grabbed sample traces for tail requests (10 traces with token_pos ~ 190). Observed a consistent ~120ms pause between token generation steps N and N+1 in the runtime timeline (on CPU side). GPU kernels show no obvious stall.
- Noted memory allocations spikes around same times on host (top-like sampling).

2025-09-27 04:30 — profiling run (Evan):
- Ran async-profiler on serving process for 2 minutes while replaying 20 long sessions in local replay harness.
- Found hot path in batching manager: function BatchScheduler::flush_if_cross_boundary().
- Flamegraph shows a thin but deep stack that corresponds to path used only when batch boundary approximation flips mid-dialog.

2025-09-27 06:00 — controlled canary compare (Diego):
- Deployed previous runtime build (pre-2025-09-27-a) to a small fraction of capacity with long-session synthetic traffic.
- Observed no latency band on pre-release deploy; present on current. Confirms regression introduced by that deploy.

Bisect plan (execution):
- We have continuous builds with hashes h1..hN. Use binary bisect across builds from 2025-09-20..2025-09-27.
- Bisect harness: containerized replay job that runs 100 synthetic long sessions (len 512 to exercise token positions 180-240), measures per-token latency heatmap and reports a single metric: fraction_of_requests_with_band (thresholded).
- Action: script bisect-builds.sh (see linked PR) — runs harness on each candidate build in ephemeral infra and returns pass/fail.
- Early bisect results: build window narrowed to two commits: commit A (introduces batching heuristics refactor) and commit B (allocator upgrade). Both touched BatchScheduler and MemoryManager.

Deep dive notes (what we profiled and why):
- CPU profiler (async-profiler) during synthetic run: captures stack traces at 1000Hz. Observed increased time in std::map rebuilds that are only hit when batch keys are rehashed — suggests boundary flips cause extra map ops.
- GPU traces: CUPTI showed no kernel queuing gap. Kernels ran back-to-back with expected durations.
- Network traces: negligible additional RTTs.
- malloc/jemalloc stats: peak RSS slightly higher in bad runs; fragmentation counters show increased arenas usage.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Most likely root cause: change in batch boundary heuristic (commit A) causes some long sessions to transition from "single continuous batch" to "split batches" near token positions ~180-240 for certain sequence-length distributions. That split triggers an extra KV-copy and a short synchronous map operation on the CPU, adding ~100-150ms intermittently to those tokens. The allocator change (commit B) exacerbates the pause by making the map reallocation costlier.

Short-term mitigations (fast):
1) Canary config change: update canary traffic profile to include long-context sessions (len >= 512) so future regressions are caught. (Owner: Maya)
2) Roll back commit A to previous batching heuristic on runtime image deployed to affected pools (if rollback safe). (Owner: Diego)
3) Add quick guard: when batch-merge boundary detected, prefer delayed non-blocking path (if available) to avoid synchronous map ops. Implement as 1-line guard in BatchScheduler for emergency build. (Owner: Priya)

Long-term fixes (defer to sprint):
- Rework batching boundary algorithm to be deterministic for long sessions — avoid mid-dialog flips — include sequence-length-aware hysteresis.
- Replace std::map usage with flat_hash_map for that hot path to reduce rehash latency variance.
- Add synthetic long-session canary and integrate heatmap diff validation into PR gating (CI).

Diagnostic queries / scripts (copy-paste candidates):
- SQL-ish pseudo to surface affected requests by token pos:
  SELECT request_id, token_pos, latency_ms FROM token_latency_samples WHERE route='route-X' AND token_pos BETWEEN 170 AND 250 ORDER BY latency_ms DESC LIMIT 200;
- replay harness command (local):
  ./replay_harness --build-image sha=commitA --profile long-session --repeat 100 --out /tmp/replay_results.json
- bisect script usage:
  ./tools/bisect-builds.sh --start 2025-09-20 --end 2025-09-27 --harness replay_harness --metric heatmap_band_fraction

Experiment logs (short):
- 2025-09-27 09:00 — rollback commit A to pool alpha: p99 improved from 420ms -> 150ms for long-session traffic. Heatmap band disappears. (quick rollback confirms commit A primary cause)
- 2025-09-27 11:00 — reapply commit A + fallback guard (BatchScheduler quick guard): p99 reduced to 160ms with rare residuals. (guard effective)
- 2025-09-27 13:00 — alternate change: replace map with folly F14 map in branch f14-map-experiment: observed lower variance but still occasional band (allocator still contributes).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Why does band always align to ~180-240 token positions across different models? Is it an emergent property of our batching policy thresholds (e.g., max_tokens_per_batch, batch alignment)? Need to inspect default values and how model tokenization variance affects effective lengths.
- Does client-side tokenization or streaming chunk sizes interact with our prefix-caching leading to boundary flips?
- Are there hardware-specific interactions (some Dedicated pools show less incidence) — need per-machine-type heatmaps.

Next steps (owners + short deadlines):
- (Maya) Add long-session synthetic traffic to canary fleet by 2025-10-05. Update canary playbook.
- (Diego) Prepare rollback + emergency release plan for commit A (if not already fully rolled back) — 2025-10-03.
- (Priya) Land quick guard patch and run perf regression tests — 2025-10-04.
- (Evan) Benchmark map replacements (flat_hash_map / folly F14) on microbench harness; report variance numbers — 2025-10-07.

Artifacts produced (for reproducibility):
- replay_results: /artifacts/heatmap-replays/run-2025-09-27.tgz
- perf traces: /artifacts/perf/async-profiler-run-2025-09-27.svg
- gpu traces: /artifacts/gpu/nsight-2025-09-27.timeline
- bisect results: /artifacts/bisect/summary-2025-09-27.txt (commit A identified)

Escalation notes (if this resurfaces after fixes):
- If rollouts reintroduce band after guard and rollback, escalate to "oncall-sre" and consider draining affected pools until full patch lands.
- For customer-impacting SLAs, enable per-request fallback to lower-latency model-variant until fix is verified.

Appendix: quick checklist for future heatmap investigations (rough):
- 1) Verify release timestamps against heatmap onset + heatmap route/model filters.
- 2) Pull sample traces (tail-focused) and CPU/GPU flamegraphs.
- 3) Run controlled replay with long-session synthetic traffic to reproduce.
- 4) Run bisect across builds if regression window > 1 build.
- 5) Check allocator and container memory stats for fragmentation spikes.
- 6) Compare canary traffic shapes — ensure long sessions included.
- 7) If batching suspicion: instrument BatchScheduler to emit boundary decisions into trace logs for 1% of traffic.
- 8) If kernel-level suspicion: capture CUPTI/Traced GPU timeline and kernel launch latencies.

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc alive until we close JIRA-1220.
- Write a short postmortem after final fix lands — include timeline and safeguard changes.

-- Priya
